newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes-Benz workers in sick-pay walk-out.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes-Benz workers in sick-pay walk-out.

text.p: Some 15,000 Mercedes-Benz workers on Thursday walked out of its largest passenger car plant in Sindelfingen near Stuttgart in protest at possible cuts in sick pay.
Employees temporarily downed tools on the early and day shifts to gather for a demonstration outside the factory gates.

The protest follows the break-down on Wednesday of talks between the IG Metall trade union and the Gesamtmetall employers federation to find agreement on proposed cuts to labour costs such as sick pay and the wider 1997 pay round.

A similar protest took place earlier this month at the Untertuerkheim plant, also near Stuttgart, after Daimler-Benz AG, Mercedes' owner, said it would be implementing a new law cutting sick pay to 80 percent of salary from the current 100 percent.
About the same number of employees as in Thursday's protest were involved. Mercedes estimated it cost some 80 million marks in lost production.
Daimler and other large engineering employers have since backed down on the cuts, saying they will wait until new work contracts can be agreed with unions.
But the companies have made it clear they see sick pay cuts or comparable measures as necessary to boost their international competitivity.
No estimate of the extent of lost production caused by Thursday's protests has yet been given.
